official.deadline_note: Annual deadline (30 November). The current call covers starts in winter semester 2026/2027, summer semester 2027 and winter semester 2027/2028.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call: deadline 30 November 2026; intake winter semester 2026/27, summer semester 2027 or winter semester 2027/28
official.status_note: The page states the annual deadline of 30 November; the current call deadline is 30 November 2026, with decisions usually communicated at the end of February.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "Waiver of study tuition fees at TU Wien" (the VCLA programme page words it as "Waiver of all tuition fees at TU Wien").
benefits: EUR 7000 annually for a duration of up to two years
Waiver of study tuition fees at TU Wien
eligibility: Female students in the field of computer science (male students are not eligible)
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or Mathematics (Bologna first cycle) or equivalent degree
Eligible for admission to one of the Master's programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English

Extensive mathematical and technical knowledge and interest in at least one of Helmut Veith's areas of research: Logic in Computer Science, Formal Methods and Verification, Foundations of Artificial Intelligence, Algorithms and Complexity Theory, Computer Security
requirements: Obtain at least 25 ECTS credits from the respective master's curriculum per term on average since the beginning of the master's studies (deadlines are April 30 for the winter term and November 30 for the summer term)
Achieve a grade average of at most 1.5
Reside in Austria during term time for the duration of the studies; exceptions and temporary interruptions are subject to approval
Funding is only awarded to applicants who have been unconditionally admitted to the Master's programme; an application for funding does not replace the admissions process
The stipend is provided for the duration of the master's programme, subject to the conditions, for up to 2 years
documents: Cover Letter describing the type of funding applied for and all other relevant aspects
Motivation Letter describing why the student wants to study in the chosen programme, why funding is necessary, and with which faculty groups the student would like to work during the master's thesis

Diplomas and/or certificates; if the final certificate is not yet available, a preliminary certificate signed and stamped by the degree-awarding university stating degree type and expected graduation date
Contact details of two referees for letters of recommendation, at least one of them from university/academia
English language certificate (TOEFL or similar), or a university confirmation of the number of semesters the candidate studied in English
Certified translation for documents that are not in German or English
selection_criteria: Selection is based on overall merit; there is no minimum GPA, but academic achievements are taken into account
Letters of recommendation are requested by the committee beginning of January
Interviews with prospective candidates are held in February
Successful candidates are usually informed at the end of February
coverage: Cash stipend of EUR 7000 per year (tax free)
Waiver of study tuition fees at TU Wien
application_method: Submit the application electronically via the TU Wien job portal (Job 270266); only applications submitted via this portal are considered and applications sent by email are deleted unread
official.application_route: Online only via the TU Wien job portal (jobs.tuwien.ac.at/Job/270266)
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published; recipients must reside in Austria during term time for the duration of their studies.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible; only graduates from accredited educational institutions are considered. Past recipients earned their bachelor's degrees in Armenia, Ukraine, Serbia, Colombia, Germany and the Netherlands.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Computer Science. Applicants must be eligible for admission to one of the English-taught CS Master's programmes; the stipend page lists Data Science, Business Informatics, Logic and Artificial Intelligence, Media and Human-Centered Computing, Software Engineering, Quantum Information Science and Technology, Embedded Computing Systems and Visual Computing (the VCLA page's list also names Medical Informatics).
official.duration: Duration of the master's programme, up to 2 years
official.description: The Helmut Veith Stipend is an annually awarded grant for female students in computer science who pursue (or plan to pursue) one of the Master's programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien taught in English, dedicated to the memory of Professor Helmut Veith (1971-2016). The fund is set up by TU Wien, the Wolfgang Pauli Institute and the colleagues and friends of the late Prof. Veith.
official.program_type: Merit-based stipend for female master's students in computer science
official.english_requirement: Proficiency in English. An English language certificate (TOEFL or similar) is required; if the candidate's bachelor studies were taught in English, a university confirmation of the number of semesters studied in English is accepted in lieu. Any English certificate accepted for admission to the chosen Master's programme is acceptable, and it may be submitted later, at the latest before commencing studies.

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage as full coverage: the VCLA page states the stipend is not a fully funded opportunity and that the amount will not suffice to cover the entire cost of living
interview and decision dates for the 2026 round beyond the published process description
verification.notes: The English stipend URL in the catalogue now returns 404 after a TU Wien site restructure; the live German-language page with identical English content, the live TU Wien job posting (Job 270266) and the VCLA programme page were used to verify the amount, benefits, conditions, documents and the 30 November 2026 deadline. The database's fully_funded flag should be corrected to false: VCLA states explicitly that the stipend is not a fully funded opportunity.

applicant_utility.summary: This stipend pays EUR 7,000 per year for up to two years plus a tuition-fee waiver at TU Wien, but it is explicitly not fully funded: the programme states the money will not cover your entire cost of living and there is no travel or accommodation allowance. You can apply before or in parallel with admission, yet the money only materialises once you are unconditionally admitted, and you must then average 25 ECTS per term with grades no worse than 1.5 while living in Austria during term time. The 2026 round closes on 30 November 2026, with referees contacted in January, interviews in February and decisions at the end of February.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Women holding a CS or Mathematics bachelor who want an English-taught technical Master's in Vienna, can document strong transcripts and English proficiency, and can commit to a fast, full-time study pace.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your eligibility for admission with the dean of academic affairs of your target Master's programme before writing anything
Line up two referees early (at least one academic), since the committee only requests letters in early January
If your final degree certificate will not exist by 30 November, order a signed and stamped preliminary certificate from your university now
Secure a TOEFL-type certificate or, if your bachelor was taught in English, the university confirmation of English-taught semesters
Book any certified translations for non-German/English documents well before the deadline
Draft the motivation letter around the specific faculty research groups you want to work with for your master's thesis
common_rejection_risks: Applying by email: only portal submissions count and emails are deleted unread
Never reaching unconditional admission: a conditional funding offer entitles you to nothing
A CV and letters that read as generic - the stipend rewards merit in Veith's own areas (logic, verification, AI foundations, algorithms, security)
A study plan that cannot sustain 25 ECTS per term at a 1.5 average, which breaks the funding conditions
Leaving the Austrian residence permit and its financial-means proof to the last minute
Assuming a second master's holder or a non-CS/mathematics bachelor fits: the profile demands a relevant first degree
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs beyond the EUR 7,000 annual stipend (the programme itself says the amount will not cover your full cost of living), accommodation, travel to and from Austria, and the financial means you must prove for the Austrian student residence permit. No travel or installation allowance is paid.
document_audit: Every non-German and non-English document needs a certified translation
A missing final certificate must be replaced by a preliminary one that is both signed and stamped and states the expected graduation date
The English certificate can arrive later, but not after your studies begin
Two referee contact details are mandatory and at least one must be academic
The motivation letter must name faculty groups, not just the programme
alerts: Deadline is a fixed calendar date (30 November) for an intake that can be winter 2026/27, summer 2027 or winter 2027/28; plan your admission timeline backwards from it
The selection clock runs January to February, so an admission decision that arrives after February leaves you waiting for next year
The stipend is tax-free only while you have no other income; part-time work can make it taxable
Recipients must stay in Austria during term time; internships or research visits need approval in advance
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an application in the TU Wien job portal (Job 270266), upload all documents by 30 November, and track the follow-up by email: referees in January, interview in February, result at the end of February.

official.deadline_note: Hard cut-off at 2 p.m. CEST on 20 October 2026; after receipt of an application, changes or the submission of missing documents are no longer possible.
official.status_note: The 2026 round is open and closes on 20 October 2026 at 2 p.m. CEST; selection takes about 4-5 months.
benefits: EUR 25,000 (super gross) for a twelve-month fellowship
The fellowship is intended to help cover living expenses
No travel or printing allowances can be applied for
eligibility: Young, highly qualified doctoral candidates pursuing doctoral studies at a university in Austria
Doctoral or PhD studies started no more than three years before the submission deadline (the deadline date is the reference point)
Not expected to need more than another twelve months to complete the doctoral thesis
Dissertation project in one of the listed subject areas: archaeology; prehistory and early history, ancient history, medieval history; art history, music history; philosophy; law
Cumulative doctorate: the publication obligation must already be fulfilled to the extent that the dissertation can be completed during the funding period
requirements: Applications can be submitted in either German or English
The programme statutes and the guidelines for good scientific practice must be observed; signing the online application form confirms the project proposal was written independently
After receipt of the application, changes or submission of missing documents are no longer possible; only formally complete applications enter the review process
Exceptions to the three-year rule (care responsibilities, illness or disability) must be clarified with the OeAW Department of Fellowships and Awards before submitting
Applications to other funding agencies are allowed but must be reported in writing to the Department of Fellowships and Awards
The fellowship must be started within three months of notification of the grant
A copy of the completed dissertation plus proof of submission for review must be supplied no later than three months after the end of the funding period
Publications resulting from the funding must carry the note "funded within the Mannagetta Fellowship Program of the OeAW"
documents: Tabular CV and list of publications

Statement of the dissertation supervisor covering the applicant's scientific qualifications, the dissertation project (question, method, significance for the field), the expected completion, and confirmation that financing from third-party funds or institute funds is not possible
Proof of previous university qualifications (Master's degree and a list of all examinations passed during the doctoral studies)

Description of the dissertation project (10-15 pages) including theoretical foundations, research question(s), preparatory work already carried out, and a detailed time and work plan for the requested funding period
Abstract of the project description in German (maximum 1-2 pages)
Upload via the online form as a total of 2 PDF files (no protected files, each file at most 10 MB), plus a scan of the signed form returned as a reply to the confirmation email
selection_criteria: Applicant's academic qualification: course and length of studies, quality and number of (peer-reviewed) publications, international mobility, grants and awards
Project: originality, innovative aspects and scientific relevance
Presentation of research questions/hypotheses and methodology
Scientific environment and qualification of supervisor(s)
Comparative assessment by the selection committee; final decision by the Mannagetta Foundation Board of Trustees, with applicants informed in writing after the board meeting
coverage: EUR 25,000 (super gross) intended to help cover living expenses
application_method: Register in the online form, prepare application and project documents, upload them as 2 PDF files, then print, sign and return the generated form by replying to the received email without changing the default subject or recipient
official.application_route: Online via the OeAW online application form for the Mannagetta Fellowship Program
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship rule is published; the applicant must be pursuing doctoral studies at a university in Austria.
official.international_eligibility: No nationality restriction is published; eligibility rests on pursuing doctoral studies at a university in Austria.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Dissertation project in archaeology; prehistory and early history, ancient history or medieval history; art history or music history; philosophy; or law.
official.research_requirement: Detailed description of the dissertation project of 10-15 pages including theoretical foundations, research question(s), preparatory work and a detailed time and work plan for the requested funding period, plus an abstract of the project description in German (maximum 1-2 pages).
official.duration: 12 months (must be started within three months of notification)
official.description: The Mannagetta Fellowships are financed from the funds of the Johann Wilhelm Ritter von Mannagetta Foundation at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and support doctoral candidates at universities in Austria in completing a doctoral thesis in archaeology, history, art and music history, philosophy or law. One or two fellowships can be granted per year.
official.program_type: Completion fellowship for doctoral candidates in the humanities, social sciences, law and arts disciplines

tuition_coverage: no tuition statement is published; the fellowship is a living-expense stipend
verification.notes: Amount (EUR 25,000 super gross), 12-month duration, the 20 October 2026 2 p.m. CEST deadline, the living-expense purpose, the exclusion of travel and printing allowances, the full document list and the selection criteria were verified on the OeAW stipendien.oeaw.ac.at pages (main, information, application and selection).

applicant_utility.summary: This is a EUR 25,000 super-gross, twelve-month completion stipend for doctoral candidates at Austrian universities in archaeology, history, art or music history, philosophy, or law, who started their doctorate no more than three years before the deadline and need at most twelve more months. It is a living-expense grant only: tuition, travel and printing are not covered, and just one or two fellowships are awarded per year. The 2026 round closes at 2 p.m. CEST on 20 October 2026, and because nothing can be added after submission, formal completeness on the day is everything.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-stage humanities, law or art-history PhD students at an Austrian university who are genuinely inside their last twelve months and whose supervisor can confirm in writing that no third-party or institute funding is available.
application_readiness_checklist: Count your doctorate's start date against the 20 October 2026 deadline to confirm the three-year rule still holds
Ask your supervisor early for the signed statement, including the no-third-party/no-institute-funding confirmation
Build the 10-15 page exposé with a month-by-month work plan that fits exactly twelve months
Write the 1-2 page abstract in German
Assemble exactly two unprotected PDFs of at most 10 MB each (application documents; project documents)
List every parallel funding application you have running so you can report it in writing
Clear any exception to the three-year rule (care, illness, disability) with the OeAW department before you submit
common_rejection_risks: Formal incompleteness: only applications meeting the formal criteria enter the review, and missing documents cannot be supplied afterwards
A supervisor statement that omits the required confirmation that third-party or institute financing is not possible
An abstract written in English rather than German
A project that visibly needs more than twelve months, or a cumulative dissertation whose publication obligation is not yet fulfilled
Protected PDF files or files above 10 MB that fail the upload
Missing the 2 p.m. CEST cut-off by hours
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, travel, printing and any project costs: the programme states that travel or printing allowances cannot be applied for, and the EUR 25,000 is intended only to help cover living expenses.
document_audit: The signed form must go back as a reply to the OeAW email with the default subject and recipient unchanged
Application and project documents travel as two separate PDF files
The supervisor statement has a mandatory content list, not just a general letter of support
Proof of previous qualifications means the Master's degree plus the full list of doctoral examinations passed
alerts: The deadline is a time of day: 20 October 2026, 2 p.m. CEST
Selection takes 4-5 months and the decision arrives in writing only after the Mannagetta Foundation Board of Trustees meets
The fellowship must start within three months of notification, so do not accept it if you cannot begin in that window
The completed dissertation plus proof of submission is due within three months after the funding period ends
Every publication from the fellowship must carry the required OeAW funding acknowledgement
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the OeAW online form, upload the two PDFs (application and project documents), then print, sign and return the generated form by replying to the confirmation email without altering its subject or recipient.
